Preserve source currentness debt for the hands-free rule and its explicitly referenced statutory exceptions. Do not turn hands-free permission into a claim of distraction-free use. Hydroplaning speeds and headlight-distance speed examples are not universal safe thresholds and remain withheld pending factual review. Physical79 requests twice-normal wet-road spacing while physical71 suggests four seconds; neither is a ceiling. The physical82 five-foot approach instruction and interpreting a withdrawn cane as an instruction to proceed require disability-safety review and are not taught. Dated age, peer-pressure, crash and texting-risk figures, including a nonofficial website statistic, remain unasserted. Image-only passing and backing diagrams are deferred. [A01] [A02] [A03] [A04] [A05] [A06] [A07] [A08]
Memory cue, authored product policy: “Pass with room, see to stop, yield to people, park the phone”. The cue retrieves complete cited rules and does not replace their conditions.
Terminology: Hydroplaning is loss of normal tire contact because of water. Visual, manual and cognitive distraction affect eyes, hands and attention respectively.
Misconception to correct: A permitted hands-free call cannot distract the driver, or a walk signal removes the driver’s need to check for people. Phone attention still matters and turning drivers must yield.
